name: Paracetamol (tab 500mg / syrup 125mg per 5ml)
dose_or_protocol: 10–15 mg/kg per dose every 6h; max 4 doses in 24h. Example (IMCI): 2–12m: 60–120mg syrup; 1–3y: 120–240mg; 4–5y: 240–360mg
how_to_use: Oral syrup or crushed tablet dissolved in water, after feeding. Never exceed max daily dose. Never give adult tablet whole to a child.
when_to_refer: Refer urgently if fever >39°C not settling, stiff neck, convulsions, lethargy, fever >5 days, or dengue warning signs
danger_signs: Convulsions; cannot drink/breastfeed; lethargic/unconscious; stiff neck

keyword_en: ORS oral rehydration salts diarrhea dehydration
name: WHO-ORS sachet (for 1 litre)
dose_or_protocol: After each loose stool: <2y: 50–100ml; 2y and above: 100–200ml; continue 3 days
how_to_use: Dissolve FULL packet in exactly 1 litre clean drinking water. Give small frequent sips. Discard solution after 24 hours.
when_to_refer: Refer urgently if sunken eyes, very sleepy/floppy, unable to drink, blood in stool, or no improvement in 3 days
danger_signs: Two or more dehydration signs = severe dehydration: give ORS and refer immediately

name: Zinc sulphate dispersible tablet (10mg / 20mg)
dose_or_protocol: <6m: 10mg once daily; 6m–5y: 20mg once daily; for FULL 14 days
how_to_use: Dissolve in water or breast milk, once daily. Continue for full 14 days even after stools stop. Give alongside ORS.
when_to_refer: Refer only if dehydration danger signs appear (see ORS row)
source_ref: WHO/UNICEF recommendation embedded in IMCI + NLEM 2022

keyword_en: IFA iron folic acid anemia blood
name: Iron + Folic Acid tablet (60mg iron + 500mcg folic acid)
dose_or_protocol: Adult/pregnant: 1 tablet daily (prophylaxis); Adolescent 10–19y: 1 tablet weekly (WIFS programme)
how_to_use: Take after food with lemon water/citrus/orange for absorption. Do NOT take with tea, coffee or milk (blocks absorption).
when_to_refer: Refer if severe palmar pallor, breathlessness at rest, or Hb <7 g/dL (severe anaemia)

name: Amoxicillin dispersible tablet 250mg
purpose: Non-severe pneumonia in children (2m–5y) — first-line per current MoHFW/WHO
dose_or_protocol: 40–50 mg/kg/day in 2 divided doses for 3–5 days. Example: 2–12m: ½ tab (125mg) twice daily; 12m–5y: 1 tab (250mg) twice daily
how_to_use: Give twice daily for the FULL course even if child improves. ONLY after classifying non-severe pneumonia in the triage engine.
when_to_refer: Refer urgently if fast breathing worsens, chest indrawing appears, or child becomes lethargic
danger_signs: Fast breathing + chest indrawing = severe pneumonia: give first dose then refer immediately
source_ref: WHO/MoHFW updated pneumonia guidance (replaces cotrimoxazole as first-line) + NLEM 2022

name: Cotrimoxazole (TMP-SMX)
purpose: Alternative antibiotic where amoxicillin unavailable, per protocol
dose_or_protocol: 4mg/kg trimethoprim twice daily for 5 days (per IMCI schedule)
how_to_use: Give twice daily for full 5 days. Only after classification by trained worker under programme protocol.
when_to_refer: Refer if danger signs appear

name: Albendazole 400mg chewable tablet
dose_or_protocol: 1–2y: 200mg single dose; 2y and above: 400mg single dose; every 6 months
how_to_use: Chew or crush with water. Single dose twice yearly on NDD.
when_to_refer: None for routine dose
source_ref: MoHFW National Deworming Day + WHO + NLEM 2022

name: Vitamin A solution (100000 / 200000 IU)
purpose: Prevents childhood blindness, measles complications, boosts immunity
dose_or_protocol: 9–11m: 100000 IU once; 12–59m: 200000 IU every 6 months (with MR vaccine); postpartum mother: 200000 IU once within 42 days (per state programme)
how_to_use: Squeeze drops directly into child's mouth. Record in immunization register.

name: Chlorhexidine 7.1% gel
purpose: Newborn cord care (per state programme protocol)
dose_or_protocol: Apply once daily to cord stump till it separates (where programme mandates)
how_to_use: Clean dry hands; apply thin layer to cord base. Keep cord clean and dry, no dressing.
when_to_refer: Refer if cord becomes red, swollen, oozing pus, or bleeds

name: Artemether-Lumefantrine (ACT) + Malaria RDT kit
purpose: Uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria treatment at community level (NVBDCP)
dose_or_protocol: Dose by weight/blisters per NVBDCP protocol (1st dose observed by ASHA, refer for completion)
how_to_use: Confirm with RDT first. Give first dose under DOTS-style observation. Complete full course. ONLY per NVBDCP training.
when_to_refer: Refer urgently if: drowsiness, repeated vomiting, convulsions, severe pallor, dark/cola urine, breathing distress, pregnancy, or infant <6 months
danger_signs: Any danger sign = severe malaria: pre-referral dose then refer immediately

name: Paracetamol paediatric syrup (125mg/5ml)
purpose: Fever in infants and young children
dose_or_protocol: 10–15 mg/kg per dose; 2–12m: 2.5–5ml (60–120mg); repeat every 6h; max 4 doses/day
how_to_use: Measure with provided dosing cup/syringe only. After feeds.
when_to_refer: Refer if fever with danger signs (see paracetamol row)

name: Condom (Nirodh)
dose_or_protocol: As needed
how_to_use: Check expiry and package integrity. Demonstrate correct use. Free supply via ASHA/ANM.

name: Levonorgestrel 1.5mg (ECP)
dose_or_protocol: 1 tablet once, as soon as possible within 72h of unprotected sex
how_to_use: One tablet orally. NOT for regular use — counsel on regular method.

name: ORS preparation method
dose_or_protocol: 1 full ORS sachet + exactly 1 litre clean water
how_to_use: Stir well. Taste should be no saltier than tears. Discard after 24h or if contaminated.
danger_signs: Wrong concentration (too salty/too weak) reduces effectiveness

name: Body temperature (digital/axillary)
dose_or_protocol: Normal: 36.5–37.5°C axillary; Fever: ≥38°C
how_to_use: Dry armpit, place bulb tip in armpit, hold arm down 2–3 min (digital beeps). For ESP32 thermal: forehead scan, add ~0.5°C offset vs axillary.
when_to_refer: Fever ≥38°C in infant <2 months = URGENT referral; high fever ≥39–40°C not settling = refer
danger_signs: Fever with stiff neck, convulsions, lethargy, non-blanching rash

name: Respiratory rate (count for 60 seconds)
dose_or_protocol: Fast breathing thresholds: 0–2m: ≥60/min; 2–12m: ≥50/min; 12–59m: ≥40/min
how_to_use: Count chest rise-fall for FULL 60 seconds when child is calm (not crying/feeding). Use the HBNC timer or app timer.
when_to_refer: Any fast-breathing threshold crossed = classify in triage engine; with chest indrawing = URGENT referral

name: MUAC tape measurement (6–59 months)
dose_or_protocol: SAM: <115mm (red zone); MAM: 115–<125mm (yellow); Normal: ≥125mm (green)
how_to_use: Measure LEFT arm midpoint (between shoulder tip and elbow tip), tape flat not tight. Read number aloud to app for voice-digitized entry.
when_to_refer: MUAC <115mm = SAM: URGENT referral to NRC; 115–<125mm = MAM: supplementary feeding referral
danger_signs: Bilateral pitting oedema (nutritional) = SAM regardless of MUAC

name: SpO₂ (pulse oximeter / ESP32 MAX30102)
purpose: Detect low blood oxygen (pneumonia, COVID, sepsis)
dose_or_protocol: Normal: 95–100%; Refer soon: <94%; URGENT: ≤90%
how_to_use: Warm the finger/hand first, insert fully, keep still 30 sec, read stable value. ESP32 sends via BLE automatically.
when_to_refer: SpO₂ <94% = refer; ≤90% = urgent referral with referral note
danger_signs: SpO₂ ≤90% with chest indrawing or lethargy = critical
source_ref: WHO IMCI severe disease guidance + MoHFW

name: Weight (infant/child scale)
purpose: Growth monitoring, drug dosing, SAM screening
dose_or_protocol: Plot on growth chart; % weight-for-age per MCP record
how_to_use: Weigh with minimal clothing, after removing soiled items. Zero the scale first. Record in app.
when_to_refer: Weight-for-age <−3 SD or sudden drop = refer; weight loss in newborn = refer
danger_signs: Very low birth weight <2.5kg needs special care referral

name: Blood pressure (digital BP monitor, BLE)
dose_or_protocol: Normal: <120/80; High BP: ≥140/90 (confirm twice); Severe: ≥160/110
how_to_use: Rest seated 5 min, arm at heart level, correct cuff size, take 2 readings 5 min apart.
when_to_refer: BP ≥160/110, or ≥140/90 with headache/chest pain/vision trouble = urgent referral; otherwise refer to CHO for confirmation
danger_signs: Severe headache, blurred vision, chest pain, breathlessness

name: Random blood sugar (glucometer)
dose_or_protocol: Normal RBS: <140 mg/dL; High: ≥200 mg/dL; Low: <70 mg/dL
how_to_use: Clean finger, prick, apply drop to strip, read. Note last meal time.
when_to_refer: RBS ≥200: refer for FBS/OGTT confirmation; <70 with sweating/shaking: give sugar/jaggery then refer if not improving

name: Hemoglobin (Hb meter via ANM/PHC)
dose_or_protocol: Anaemia adult/preg: <11 g/dL; Severe: <7 g/dL
how_to_use: Finger-prick Hb meter reading by trained worker (ANM); ASHA refers suspect cases.
when_to_refer: Hb <7 g/dL, or <11 with symptoms (breathlessness, chest pain) = referral
danger_signs: Severe pallor with breathlessness at rest

name: Malaria rapid diagnostic test (RDT)
dose_or_protocol: Positive/negative band reading per kit insert
how_to_use: Finger-prick blood sample on RDT, wait 15–20 min, read bands. Record result. Only NVBDCP-trained use.
when_to_refer: Positive with any danger sign = urgent referral; negative but febrile >7 days = refer

name: Fever home care
purpose: What to do for simple fever before/alongside referral decision
dose_or_protocol: Paracetamol as dosed + plenty of fluids + tepid sponging if hot
how_to_use: Keep child cool, remove excess clothing, offer breast milk/fluids frequently. Watch for danger signs every few hours.
when_to_refer: Fever >5 days, >39°C not settling, or any danger sign = refer
danger_signs: Convulsions; stiff neck; non-blanching rash; lethargy

name: Cough/cold home care
purpose: Relieve simple cough and blocked nose
dose_or_protocol: No medicine needed for simple cold
how_to_use: Normal feeds, keep warm, saline nose drops, gentle steam. Raise head while sleeping.
when_to_refer: Refer if: fast breathing, chest indrawing, stridor, cough >14 days (TB screen), blood in sputum
danger_signs: Fast breathing; chest indrawing; stridor at rest

name: Diarrhoea — continue feeding
dose_or_protocol: Continue and increase breastfeeding; give soft familiar foods
how_to_use: Small frequent feeds; extra fluids (ORS); zinc 14 days.
when_to_refer: Danger signs per ORS row

name: Dengue — warning signs
purpose: Recognize dengue before it becomes severe
how_to_use: Fever with any of: severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, bleeding gums/nose, black stools, restlessness, cold hands, skin rash. Encourage fluids; paracetamol ONLY.
when_to_refer: ANY warning sign = URGENT referral. NO aspirin/ibuprofen (bleeding risk)
danger_signs: Bleeding; severe abdominal pain; persistent vomiting; lethargy

name: Malaria prevention
how_to_use: Sleep under insecticide-treated nets (ITN), especially children/pregnant; drain stagnant water; fever in monsoon = test early.
when_to_refer: Any fever in endemic season: RDT; danger signs = urgent referral

name: Exclusive breastfeeding
dose_or_protocol: Exclusive breast milk till 6 months — no water, no ghutti, no formula needed
how_to_use: Feed on demand day/night; correct latching; mother's nutrition important.
when_to_refer: If baby not feeding well = danger sign, refer

name: Kangaroo Mother Care
dose_or_protocol: Skin-to-skin contact as many hours/day as possible
how_to_use: Baby in diaper only, upright on mother's chest inside her clothing, head turned to side, cover with cloth/blanket.
when_to_refer: If baby cold to touch, not feeding, or lethargic = URGENT referral

name: Antenatal care schedule
dose_or_protocol: Minimum 4 ANC checkups; IFA daily; TT as scheduled; register on MCP card; birth preparedness by month 7
how_to_use: App due-date engine reminds visits. Counseling on nutrition, danger signs, institutional delivery plan.
when_to_refer: ANY pregnancy danger sign = immediate referral (see P02)

name: Birth preparedness
purpose: Plan so delivery is not delayed
dose_or_protocol: Identify facility + transport + blood donor + emergency money in advance
how_to_use: Fill the birth plan in app by 7th month; keep PHC/108 numbers offline; pack bag in advance.
when_to_refer: Any labour before 9 months, or danger signs = go immediately

name: Handwashing & hygiene
how_to_use: Soap + running water, 40–60 seconds, before feeding/after toilet. Safe drinking water storage.

name: UIP immunization schedule
dose_or_protocol: Birth: BCG+OPV0+HepB; 6/10/14wk: Pentavalent+OPV+Rotavirus+PCV; 9–12m: MR1+VitA (+JE1 in endemic); 16–24m: MR2+DPTb1+OPVb (+JE2); 5–6y: DPTb2
how_to_use: Follow due-list from app engine; check contraindications (fever mild = NOT a contraindication); record every dose.
when_to_refer: Missed doses: catch-up at next session; refer if vaccine-preventable disease suspected

name: TB symptom screen
dose_or_protocol: Cough >2 weeks, fever >2 weeks, weight loss, night sweats, blood in sputum = TB suspect
how_to_use: Ask the 4 questions in app; if suspect: refer for sputum test (Ni-kshay), do NOT start any medicine yourself.
when_to_refer: All TB suspects = refer to PHC for sputum/Ni-kshay registration

name: Family planning counselling
dose_or_protocol: Spacing methods: condoms, OCPs, emergency pill (backup only); refer for long-term methods (IUCD, injectables) at PHC
how_to_use: Counsel respectfully, privacy matters; provide condoms/ECP from kit; refer for other methods.

name: Adolescent anaemia (WIFS)
dose_or_protocol: 1 IFA tablet (45mg iron) weekly + screen for anaemia
how_to_use: Weekly dose every Monday with citrus; deworming twice yearly.
when_to_refer: Pallor + weakness = Hb test referral

name: GENERAL DANGER SIGN — not able to drink or breastfeed
how_to_use: Do not force feed. Position comfortably. Prepare for referral.
when_to_refer: URGENT referral — do not wait or observe further

name: GENERAL DANGER SIGN — vomits everything
how_to_use: Give nothing by mouth temporarily; small ORS sips only if tolerated; refer.
when_to_refer: URGENT referral
danger_signs: Persistent vomiting + abdominal pain in fever season = possible dengue

name: GENERAL DANGER SIGN — convulsions
how_to_use: Turn on side, clear surroundings, NOTHING in mouth, time the episode.
when_to_refer: URGENT referral after episode ends

name: GENERAL DANGER SIGN — lethargic or unconscious
how_to_use: Do not attempt home care; keep airway clear; refer.
when_to_refer: URGENT referral

name: Severe pneumonia sign — chest indrawing
how_to_use: Give first antibiotic dose if trained, then refer immediately — do NOT wait.
when_to_refer: URGENT referral
danger_signs: With fast breathing and SpO₂ <94% = critical

name: Fast breathing thresholds
dose_or_protocol: 0–2m ≥60/min; 2–12m ≥50/min; 12–59m ≥40/min (count 60 sec, calm child)
how_to_use: Use app timer; count twice if unsure.
when_to_refer: Any threshold crossed = triage classification; with indrawing = urgent

name: Blood in stool (dysentery)
how_to_use: Continue feeding and ORS; do not give anti-diarrhoeal medicines.
when_to_refer: Refer for assessment (antibiotic per protocol after evaluation)

name: Sunken eyes + signs of dehydration
dose_or_protocol: Check: sunken eyes, skin pinch returns slowly, restless/irritable, thirsty, no urine 6h+
how_to_use: Skin pinch on belly 1 sec; if slow return = dehydration.
when_to_refer: 2+ signs or any severe sign = URGENT referral with ORS during travel
danger_signs: Very sleepy, floppy, unable to drink = SEVERE dehydration

name: Stridor (harsh breathing sound at rest)
how_to_use: Keep calm (crying worsens it); cool mist air.
when_to_refer: Stridor at rest = URGENT referral; with drooling/high fever = emergency
danger_signs: Drooling + unable to swallow = epiglottitis emergency

name: Severe palmar pallor
dose_or_protocol: Check inner lower eyelid and palm vs yours
how_to_use: If conjunctiva/palm very pale — do not wait for Hb.
when_to_refer: URGENT referral (Hb <7 likely)

name: Pregnancy danger signs — bleeding
how_to_use: Any bleeding in pregnancy = emergency. Keep flat; arrange transport via 108.
when_to_refer: IMMEDIATE referral/108 — do not wait

name: Pregnancy danger signs — severe headache, blurred vision, face/hand swelling, convulsions
how_to_use: Measure BP if possible; note swelling; keep calm, left-side lying.
when_to_refer: IMMEDIATE referral/108

name: Reduced/absent fetal movement
how_to_use: Count movements after meal; <10 in 12h = concerning.
when_to_refer: Same-day urgent referral

name: Newborn danger signs (0–2 months): not feeding well
how_to_use: Attempt feed; if refuses repeatedly or too weak to suck = danger.
when_to_refer: URGENT referral — neonates deteriorate fast

name: Newborn danger signs: RR ≥60, chest indrawing, fever/hypothermia, jaundice to palms/soles, cord/skin infection, lethargy
how_to_use: Check temperature, RR (60s), cord, skin, activity at every HBNC visit.
when_to_refer: ANY one sign = URGENT referral immediately

name: Snakebite first response
how_to_use: Keep patient STILL, remove tight items, immobilize limb at heart level; NO cutting/sucking/tourniquet/herbs. Mark swelling edge with pen.
when_to_refer: URGENT referral — antivenom only at hospital; call 108. Transport the patient, not the snake (photo ok)
danger_signs: Drooping eyelids, bleeding, breathing difficulty = severe envenomation

name: Poisoning/overdose first response
how_to_use: Do NOT induce vomiting; rinse mouth; keep container/sample for doctor; if unconscious = side position.
when_to_refer: URGENT referral with the container

name: ERSS-112 (pan-India emergency)
how_to_use: Dial 112 for police/fire/medical emergencies; works on zero-balance SIM; location-assisted.

name: 108 / 102 Referral Transport
how_to_use: 108 = medical emergency; 102 = pregnant woman/child referral transport (Janani express in many states); keep number offline in app.

name: Janani Suraksha Yojana
dose_or_protocol: Mother: cash assistance (rural ~₹1400 general / ₹1600 SC-ST in most states); ASHA: ~₹600 per rural institutional delivery escort
how_to_use: Register pregnancy early; accompany/arrange transport; submit voucher via app stub.

name: Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram
purpose: Free drugs, diet, diagnostics, blood for pregnant women + sick infants up to 1 year
how_to_use: At any government facility: no charges for delivery, C-section, drugs, diet, diagnostics, blood, or newborn treatment. Tell the family to demand it.

name: PM-JAY (Ayushman Bharat)
how_to_use: Check family eligibility via ration card/Aadhaar at empaneled hospital; scan Ayushman card QR in app.

name: Nutrition Rehabilitation Centre
how_to_use: SAM (MUAC <115mm or bilateral oedema) = NRC admission for therapeutic feeding; free under programme.

name: PMBJP Janaushadhi Kendra
how_to_use: Show nearest Kendra from offline map POI; verify prices at janaushadhi.gov.in price list.

name: Ni-kshay / NTEP TB programme
purpose: Free TB diagnosis, drugs + ₹500/month nutrition support (NPY)
how_to_use: Refer suspect for sputum test; if confirmed, ensure registration on Ni-kshay; support adherence visits (DOTS).

name: VHSND (Village Health Sanitation & Nutrition Day)
purpose: Monthly village outreach: immunization, ANC, nutrition, counseling
how_to_use: App calendar shows this month's VHSND date/venue; remind all due beneficiaries 2 days before.

name: ABHA (Ayushman Bharat Health Account)
how_to_use: Scan patient's ABHA QR to auto-fill identity; create via Aadhaar OTP when online at PHC.

name: MCP Card (Mother & Child Protection)
how_to_use: Record ANC visits, IFA, TT, birth outcome on MCP; app's due-engine mirrors the card.

name: Anemia Mukt Bharat
purpose: National anaemia control programme (6 target groups)
how_to_use: IFA prophylaxis per group (daily adults, weekly adolescents); test-and-treat at PHC.

name: Incentive voucher claim (PFMS/ASHA Soft)
dose_or_protocol: Varies by state (JSY ~₹600, full immunization ~₹100, HBYC ~₹250 per schedule, etc.)
how_to_use: App auto-generates voucher on task completion; track pending claims in app; submit at monthly sector meeting.
when_to_refer: Payment pending >45 days = flag to Facilitator via dashboard

name: NEVER give aspirin to children
how_to_use: Use only paracetamol for fever in children.

name: NEVER give honey to infants under 1 year
how_to_use: No honey, no ghutti, no water for <6 months — breast milk only.

name: NEVER give antibiotics without classification
how_to_use: Run the triage assessment first; antibiotics only for classified non-severe pneumonia etc.

name: NEVER use leftover/shared medicines
how_to_use: Each illness gets fresh assessment and correct dosing from the kit.

name: NO cough syrups/steroids for children (unless prescribed)
purpose: No benefit, real harm in children
how_to_use: Simple cold needs no medicine; persistent cough >14 days = TB screen referral.

name: Iron absorption warning
how_to_use: Take IFA with water + citrus (lemon/orange/aamla), never with tea or milk.

name: ORS solution expires in 24 hours
how_to_use: Make fresh daily; discard leftover; wash container.

name: Never stop antibiotics/zinc mid-course
how_to_use: Amoxicillin full 3–5 days; zinc full 14 days — even if child seems fully recovered.

name: Snakebite — no cutting, sucking, tourniquet, ice, herbs
how_to_use: Immobilize + transport to hospital with antivenom. Photo of snake if safe.

name: WHEN IN DOUBT — REFER
purpose: The golden rule of community health
how_to_use: This guide supports but never replaces the triage engine. If unsure after assessment: refer.
